reasons: Claimed status is compliant with no redline or comment, which is the expected output shape; nothing is raised with the counterparty, so there is no over-flagging risk.

The cited text supports the conclusion: Section 10.2 contains a substantive express representation/warranty package from Harpoon (the counterparty), Section 3.8.4 imposes a performance standard ('good scientific manner and in compliance with all Applicable Law') and Section 10.3.3 requires appropriately qualified personnel — the deal-type analogues of the professional/workmanlike and compliance-with-laws elements.

The Section 10.5 disclaimer expressly opens with 'EXCEPT FOR THE EXPRESS WARRANTIES SET FORTH HEREIN', so it does not swallow the express warranties; the clause is clearly not at the 'AS IS' walk-away position.

The failed deterministic check (no 90-day/12-month conformance window) is correctly treated as an inapplicable sub-element rather than a deviation: this is a drug development and option collaboration with no software or services deliverables to conform to documentation, and the rationale flags the absence explicitly instead of hiding it.

Rationale is accurate in citing remedy pathways actually present in this deal type (material-breach/step-in mechanics, indemnification, termination on debarment) rather than inventing a repair/replace/refund remedy.
